title: Compatible finite chain maps assemble uniquely on the sequence site
statement: Let C carry a Grothendieck topology J and satisfy the coefficient-universe smallness, sheafification and module-sheaf composition hypotheses of [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. For a sequence B of commutative ring sheaves, let X,Y be cochain complexes of modules on its ringed sequence site. A family f_n of maps between their vertical evaluations, commuting degreewise with every horizontal semilinear transition, comes from exactly one chain map X to Y. The additive structure used to map these complexes is the existing vertical-evaluation structure of [lem-pur-system-evaluation-topos].

source.place: Tag 0941, modules on the ringed sequence site; strict-system equivalence of lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site

proof.text: Use the existing additive vertical-evaluation instance from lem-pur-system-evaluation-topos to map cochain complexes. In every degree the maps f_n form a strict-system morphism by the given horizontal equation. Their differential equations hold at every level, hence by strictRingSystem_hom_ext hold as system morphisms.

Use full faithfulness of strictSystemSequenceEquivalence.inverse to lift each degree map. Map the differential equation through this faithful functor and use map_preimage to prove the chain equation. Evaluating map_preimage gives the prescribed components. Any other lift agrees levelwise and therefore degreewise by faithfulness, proving uniqueness.

lean.statement:
theorem sequenceComplexHom_existsUnique
    (X Y : CochainComplex (systemSequenceModules B) ℤ)
    (f : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((systemSequenceEvaluation B n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj X ⟶
        ((systemSequenceEvaluation B n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Y)
    (hf : ∀ (i : ℤ) {m n : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n),
      (f n).f i ≫ sequenceSystemTransition B (Y.X i) h =
        sequenceSystemTransition B (X.X i) h ≫ (systemRestriction B h).map ((f m).f i)) :
    ∃! g : X ⟶ Y, ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((systemSequenceEvaluation B n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map g = f n
